title: Add the Eleventh Cache Node
description: A balanced ten-node cache uses a consistent hash ring. An equal-capacity eleventh node joins. Roughly what share of keys should move on average?

options.text: All keys, because the membership count changed.
options.explanation: That resembles modulo rehashing. A ring changes ownership only for the joining node's ranges.

options.text: Exactly one half, regardless of node count.
options.explanation: Movement depends on the new node's expected ownership share, not a fixed half.

options.text: About 1/11, with actual movement depending on placement.
options.explanation: With balanced ownership, the new node takes about one share out of eleven. This is an expectation, not an exact guarantee.

options.text: No keys, because existing owners never change.
options.explanation: The new node must acquire ranges to hold its share; otherwise it contributes no cache capacity.
